---
title: "How do I test whether two categories are associated?"
---

## Question

How do I test whether two categories are associated?

## Decide which method fits

Construct a contingency table of counts, weighting summarized rows if necessary; inspect expected counts; use chi-square or a suitable exact method and interpret association carefully.

## Worked example: Titanic

```{r}
#| eval: false
d <- ru_data("Titanic")
fit <- ru_apply("categorical_independence", d,
                x="Sex", y="Survived", weight="Freq")
stopifnot(!is.null(fit))
```

The Titanic dataset stores historical counts in aggregated rows. Weighting by Freq is essential; treating each aggregated row as one person would give the wrong contingency table. Historical counts are not automatically a random sample from a broader population.

## Apply to another dataset

```r
ru_apply("categorical_independence", your_data, x="category_A", y="category_B", weight="frequency_column")
```

If expected counts are small, the code uses Fisher's exact test for a 2×2 table or declines to select an unreliable chi-square approximation for a larger sparse table.

Review assumptions and available input conditions with `ru_plan("categorical_independence")`. A valid computation does not itself verify the underlying study design.
